A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TabPFN-TS using TabPFN-v2. All 23 pages of v3 and 26 pages of v4, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Renamed and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original TabPFN-TS forecasting results on GIFT-Eval, synthetic experiments, and feature, context-length, and CatBoost backbone ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains original forecasting results and adds fev-bench evaluation, controlled synthetic covariate experiments, and TabDPT-TS results.

M1.justification: V4 Section 3.1 appends time-varying covariates known throughout the forecast horizon to the temporal features; v3 left incorporating covariates to future work. This is a limited input extension: the calendar, seasonal and index features, TabPFN-v2 backbone, and forecasting procedure remain.

E1.justification: V4 adds evaluation on 28 fev-bench tasks requiring known historical and future covariates. It also adds ten synthetic covariate classes combining additive or multiplicative effects with trends, pulses, ramps, random walks and composite signals. The original 97 GIFT-Eval tasks remain.

E2.justification: The main GIFT-Eval comparison adds TiRex, Toto-1.0, Moirai-2 and Sundial-Base, while removing Chronos-Bolt-Small and Tiny from that comparison, although they remain elsewhere. The backbone ablation replaces CatBoost-TS with TabDPT-TS. Timing comparisons replace Chronos-Bolt-Small/Tiny with Chronos-Bolt-Base and TimesFM-2.0.

E3.justification: Added protocols include selecting 28 of 30 eligible fev-bench tasks after six-hour timeouts, evaluating TabDPT on 78 of 97 GIFT-Eval tasks using point forecasts, and comparing covariates-present versus covariates-absent conditions. V4 also introduces GPU-count-normalized timing comparisons. The original GIFT-Eval accuracy metrics and aggregation remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds controlled tests of when covariates help, including additive versus multiplicative effects and extrapolation failures. It replaces the classical-regressor CatBoost ablation with a TabDPT study of transfer across foundation backbones. V3's single-feature, 64-harmonic appendix plots are removed; feature, context-length and two-feature harmonic analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: V4 introduces boxplots showing the spread of MASE and WQL improvements within synthetic covariate classes in Figure 5.4. Existing GIFT-Eval 95% confidence intervals remain. Neither version specifies seeds, repeated-run counts or confidence-interval construction, so increased replication is not established.

E6.justification: TabPFN-TS's GIFT-Eval relative WQL/MASE remain 0.460/0.692, while mean WQL rank changes from 3.680 to 5.392 with revised comparator membership. New results include 0.503 WQL/0.666 MASE on 28 fev-bench tasks and TabDPT-TS MASE of 0.755 on 78 GIFT-Eval tasks; these are not same-setting improvements over v3. V3's per-task accuracy and runtime tables disappear, while new covariate and timing findings appear.

T1.justification: V4 extends the formal forecasting distribution and feature definition to include covariates. V3 Section 5.2's explicit sin(4x) polynomial identity and Chebyshev-style harmonic argument are removed. Calendar and Fourier definitions remain substantively unchanged, and no formal theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V3's title and central claims emphasize surpassing specialized forecasting models and leading GIFT-Eval. V4 narrows this to competitive univariate performance, while introducing state-of-the-art covariate-informed forecasting and generalization across tabular foundation backbones as central contributions.

C2.justification: V4 interprets seasonal forecasting as interpolation in phase features and attributes extrapolation limitations to pretraining. It replaces v3's relatively favorable interpretation of exponential trends with a broader extrapolation-failure interpretation of retained plots. It also explains known-future-covariate requirements and inference costs arising from separate passes per series and quadratic attention.

D1.justification: V4 adds a precise checkpoint link and clarifies missing-observation filtering, context selection and internal normalization in Appendix A.3. It drops v3's power-transformed-target ensemble disclosure, CatBoost configuration table and composite-signal parameter ranges. Much configuration information is relocated; omitted details do not establish changes to the executed pipeline.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused toward contemporary time-series foundation models, covariate conditioning and alternative tabular foundation backbones. Added works include TiRex, Toto, Sundial, COSMIC, TabDPT, TabArena and fev-bench, while much of v3's discussion and citations concerning classical forecasting, boosted trees and earlier model development are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and substantial portions of the methodology, interpretation and conclusion are rewritten. Ablations are reordered, configuration moves into the appendix, a separate limitations section is created, and author information is updated.

P2.justification: V4 changes typography, margins and author layout, expands the overview diagram with covariates, and adds benchmark, synthetic, backbone and timing plots. Model-size, raw accuracy, raw runtime and CatBoost configuration tables are removed; a fev-bench task table is added. Several retained figures are relocated or redrawn.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens the paper through broader comparisons, a better-calibrated univariate claim, and real-data plus controlled evidence for covariate use. These gains are tempered by removing per-task accuracy/runtime tables and reproducibility details. Moreover, Figure 4.2 identifies TabPFN-TS as the only compared model with direct covariate support, limiting the breadth of the new leadership claim. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
